extracted.intended_audience: U.S. Patent and Trademark Office patent examiners (primary); patent practitioners and applicants (secondary)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for evaluating and processing Requests for Continued Examination (RCE) filed under 37 CFR 1.114: eligibility, required fee and submission content, effects on appeals and allowance, entering submissions, timing/shortened reply periods, new matter and switching-invention rules, and comparisons with CPA/URAA procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for RCE under 37 CFR 1.114
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for continued examination under 37 CFR 1.114, the application must be a utility or plant application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) on or after June 8, 1995, or an international application filed under 35 U.S.C. 363 on or after June 8, 1995. The RCE must be filed on or after May 29, 2000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeated as a prerequisite throughout (see multiple Examiner Notes). RCE practice not applicable to provisional applications, design applications, applications filed before June 8, 1995, or during reexamination. If application does not meet eligibility, use Form PTO-2051 (Notice of Improper Request for Continued Examination).

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE must include required fee and submission
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for continued examination under 37 CFR 1.114 must include the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(e) and a submission as required by 37 CFR 1.114.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the fee and/or submission is missing the RCE is improper; consequences vary (e.g., withdrawal of appeal and abandonment, or passing to issue on allowed claims). Examiner should use the appropriate form paragraph (e.g., 7.42.16) to notify applicant. In some circumstances a submission filed with an improper RCE should not be entered, except in narrow situations (see exception below).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission must be a bona fide attempt to advance the application
rubrics_metrics.description: A submission under 37 CFR 1.114 must include a reply that is a bona fide attempt to advance the application (per 37 CFR 1.111) if a reply to an Office action is outstanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a submission appears not fully responsive to the prior Office action but is a bona fide attempt to provide a complete reply, the examiner gives applicant a shortened statutory period of ONE MONTH (or THIRTY DAYS, whichever is longer) to submit a complete reply; this period may be extended under 37 CFR 1.136(a). Use form paragraph 7.42.08 to acknowledge an RCE with a submission that is not fully responsive.

rubrics_metrics.name: No new matter allowed in amendments submitted under 1.114
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 132(a) provides that 'No amendment shall introduce new matter into the disclosure of the invention.' Any amendment entered pursuant to 37 CFR 1.114 that is determined to contain new matter should be treated as a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 determined to contain new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant seeks to add new matter to the disclosure, the 1.114 procedure is not available; applicant must file a continuation-in-part under 37 CFR 1.53(b). See MPEP § 706.03(o) for treatment of new matter. Examiner must handle amendments containing new matter consistently with 37 CFR 1.111 practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cannot switch inventions via RCE (no switching-invention)
rubrics_metrics.description: Because 35 U.S.C. 132(b) and 37 CFR 1.114 provide continued examination of an application (and not examination of a continuing application), the applicant cannot file an RCE to obtain continued examination on claims that are independent and distinct from the claims previously claimed and examined as a matter of right (i.e., applicant cannot switch inventions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.145 and MPEP discussion. If applicant seeks to pursue a different invention, a divisional or other appropriate filing may be required; RCE is not the vehicle to switch inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of an RCE filed after appeal but before Board decision
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant files an RCE under 37 CFR 1.114 after filing a Notice of Appeal to the Board but prior to a decision, it will be treated as a request to withdraw the appeal and to reopen prosecution (37 CFR 1.114(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should advise the Board when an RCE is filed; otherwise the Board may refuse to vacate a decision rendered after filing of an RCE but before recognition by the Office. Use form paragraphs 7.42.06 (after appeal but before Board decision) or 7.42.10–7.42.14 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE filed after Board decision but before further appeal/civil action
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing an RCE (with fee and submission) after a decision by the Board but before filing a Notice of Appeal to the Federal Circuit or commencing a civil action will result in withdrawal of the decision's finality and reopening of prosecution if the fee has been timely paid and submission entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Board decision has res judicata effect and is 'law of the case'; therefore, a submission containing only arguments without amendment or new facts will not remove such rejection. Use form paragraph 7.42.07 to notify applicant that appeal has been withdrawn and prosecution reopened. See MPEP §§ 706.03(w), 1214.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper RCE after Board decision (missing fee/submission)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an RCE is filed after a Board decision but before further appeal/civil action and it lacks the fee and/or submission, the RCE is improper and any time period running was not tolled by the filing of the improper request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should notify applicant using form paragraph 7.42.16. If time for seeking court review has passed, include this paragraph with Notice of Allowability or Notice of Abandonment as appropriate; if time remains, include it on a PTOL-90. Generally do not enter the submission; exception: an amendment that obviously places the application in condition for allowance may be entered with supervisory approval (MPEP § 1214.07).

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE filed after allowance or Quayle reopens prosecution (when fee & submission included)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant files an RCE (including the fee and a submission) in an application which has been allowed or had an Office action under Ex parte Quayle, prosecution will be reopened.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the issue fee has already been paid, filing an RCE and submission without a petition under 37 CFR 1.313 will not avoid issuance. If RCE is filed before payment of the issue fee, a petition under 1.313 is not required. Use form paragraph 7.42.05 to notify applicant that prosecution has been reopened. If RCE filed after issue fee paid and petition granted, applicant need not pay issue fee again if application is thereafter allowed; no refund available if prosecution reopens.

rubrics_metrics.name: First action following RCE may be final only under specified conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The action immediately subsequent to the filing of an RCE with a submission and fee under 37 CFR 1.114 may be made final only if the conditions set forth in MPEP § 706.07(b) for making a first action final in a continuing application are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 7.42.09 is to be used where appropriate to make the first action after filing an RCE final. When used, set a shortened statutory period for reply to expire THREE MONTHS from the mailing date; special rules apply if a first reply is filed within TWO MONTHS and the advisory action timing (see paragraph text).

rubrics_metrics.name: When a submission filed with an improper RCE may be entered
rubrics_metrics.description: In general, if a submission was filed with an improper RCE it should not be entered. An exception exists for an amendment which obviously places the application in condition for allowance — such an amendment may be entered with supervisory approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should include a statement whether any such submission has been entered (e.g., 'The submission filed with the improper RCE has not been entered.'). See MPEP § 1214.07 for guidance and consult supervisory patent examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE filed after appeal but without submission/fee — abandonment if no allowed claims
rubrics_metrics.description: If an RCE was filed after appeal to the Board but the request lacks the fee and/or required submission, and no claim is allowed, the proceedings as to the rejected claims are terminated and the application is abandoned (see form paragraph 7.42.10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.42.10 to withdraw the appeal and hold the application abandoned where appropriate. See MPEP § 1215.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE filed after appeal with fee but lacking submission — pass to issue on allowed claims
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for continued examination filed after appeal that includes the fee but lacks the submission will result in withdrawal of the appeal and the application being passed to issue on allowed claim(s). Claims indicated as containing allowable subject matter but dependent on a rejected claim are to be canceled (form paragraph 7.42.11).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert claim numbers in brackets as required and cancel dependent claims as if rejected per MPEP § 1215.01. Use appropriate form paragraph with Notice of Allowability when passing to issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE filed after appeal with fee but lacking submission — allowed claim with formal matters outstanding
rubrics_metrics.description: When an RCE filed after appeal includes the fee but lacks the required submission, and there is at least one allowed claim but formal matters remain outstanding, the application will be passed to issue on the allowed claim provided the formal matters are corrected within a shortened statutory period of ONE MONTH (or THIRTY DAYS, whichever is longer) from mailing date; extensions per 37 CFR 1.136 may be granted (form paragraph 7.42.12).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In form paragraph bracket explain formal matters to be corrected. If not timely corrected, prosecution is otherwise closed. See MPEP § 1215.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE filed after appeal including submission but lacking fee — submission not entered; pass to issue on allowed claims
rubrics_metrics.description: If an RCE filed after appeal includes a submission but lacks the fee required by 37 CFR 1.17(e), the submission has not been entered (see 37 CFR 1.116(c)). Since proceedings as to rejected claims are terminated, the application will be passed to issue on allowed claim(s) (form paragraph 7.42.13).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert claim numbers and cancel dependent claims as appropriate. If formal matters outstanding, use form paragraph 7.42.14 to require corrections within shortened statutory period.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE filed after appeal including submission but lacking fee — allowed claim with formal matters outstanding
rubrics_metrics.description: If an RCE filed after appeal includes a submission but lacks the fee and there are allowed claims with outstanding formal matters, the application will be passed to issue on allowed claims provided the formal matters are corrected within ONE MONTH or THIRTY DAYS (whichever is longer) from mailing date; extensions per 37 CFR 1.136 may be granted (form paragraph 7.42.14).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket explain the formal matters to be corrected. If not corrected, prosecution is otherwise closed. See MPEP § 1215.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE fee amount and excess-claims policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office sets the RCE fee at an amount equal to the basic filing fee of a utility application (small entity reduction available). The RCE fee need not include excess claims fees for claims previously paid for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is stated in the comparison chart among CPA, URAA, and RCE. Fee handling details (small entity reduction, excess claims) should be applied consistent with prevailing fee schedules and 37 CFR 1.17(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of RCE on patent term adjustment (PTA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing an RCE on or after May 29, 2000 will not cause an application to be entitled to patent term adjustment provisions of the AIPA. If an application is already entitled to PTA, filing an RCE cuts off the applicant's ability to accumulate any additional PTA against the three-year pendency provision but does not otherwise affect PTA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See comparison chart notes. Filing an RCE may affect accumulation of PTA toward three-year pendency; consult appropriate PTA guidance when processing RCEs filed on/after May 29, 2000.

rubrics_metrics.name: No limit on number of RCEs
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no limit on the number of times an applicant may file an RCE to obtain continued examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrast with CPA and URAA transitional procedures which have limits on submissions entered as a matter of right. Track multiple RCEs and related fee/payment history per Office policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE entitled to Certificate of Mailing
rubrics_metrics.description: An RCE is entitled to the benefit of a Certificate of Mailing under 37 CFR 1.8.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare with CPA (not entitled) and URAA submissions (entitled) in the comparison chart. Ensure Certificate of Mailing procedures are followed where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission in national stage (§ 371) remains subject to unity of invention
rubrics_metrics.description: If a submission is filed in a national stage application under 35 U.S.C. § 371, the application is still subject to unity of invention practice in accordance with 37 CFR 1.475 and 1.499.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unity/restriction practice continues to apply even when an RCE or submission is filed in a national stage application; follow relevant restriction and unity rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison of CPA, URAA (37 CFR 1.129(a)), and RCE (37 CFR 1.114)
rubrics_metrics.description: The RCE procedure under 37 CFR 1.114 differs from CPA (37 CFR 1.53(d)) and URAA transitional practice (37 CFR 1.129(a)) in applicability, statutory authority, fee structure, patent term adjustment effects, limits on number of submissions, and other procedural effects (e.g., whether filing abandons prior application, entitlement to Certificate of Mailing, whether submission must be after final, whether small entity status carries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided comparison chart to determine which procedure applies and the practical/legal consequences (e.g., CPA may be filed before prosecution closed; URAA practice applies only to applications filed before or on June 8, 1995; RCE must generally be filed after prosecution closed; differences in fee deferral and PTA consequences are described in the chart).

rubrics_metrics.name: Switching inventions and adding new matter — common prohibition across procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may not switch inventions (divisional equivalent) or add new matter (CIP equivalent) as a matter of right under CPA, URAA, or RCE practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The chart emphasizes that CPA, URAA, and RCE practice do not permit switching inventions or adding new matter as a matter of right; practitioners must use proper continuation/divisional/CIP procedures where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small entity status carryover varies by procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Small entity status treatment differs: CPA practice does not automatically carry small entity status (but may be claimed by reference or payment), URAA transitional practice carries/continues small entity status, and RCE practice carries/continues small entity status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners and applicants must verify and apply the correct small entity status rules based on which procedure (CPA, URAA, RCE) is used and the relevant filings/payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE must generally be filed after prosecution is closed (post-August 16, 2000)
rubrics_metrics.description: After August 16, 2000, an RCE must be filed after the prosecution in an application is closed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This timing distinction is highlighted in the comparison chart versus CPA and URAA. Ensure prosecution status is closed before accepting an RCE filed on/after that date.
